summary: Table gains `layout="auto"` and a real scroll region. An adversarial review flagged the table as not responsive, and the investigation corrected the premise on the way: `width` was ALREADY optional on every column — the colgroup only emits one where it is declared — so a table with no widths has always rendered. What it did was split the space EQUALLY, because `table-fixed` was hard-coded, so an ID lane and a name lane got the same room. The sharper finding was underneath it: the frame was `overflow-clip`, so a grid wider than its container lost its right-hand columns SILENTLY, with no scrollbar and no affordance. That was in knownGaps ("wrap it yourself if you need a scroll container") and it is the worse half of the two — squeezing is ugly, clipping loses data. `overflow-x-auto` fixes it and keeps the concentric corner, because any non-visible overflow clips at the border box. `fixed` stays the DEFAULT against the ecosystem's grain (shadcn, Radix Themes, Carbon and Primer all default to auto) for a reason those libraries do not have: lane agreement across the header, the rows, the skeleton and the empty state is the whole point of the lane system, and under `auto` the lanes move when the data lands because the skeleton's placeholder text is not the data's. The scroll region is a tab stop ONLY while it actually scrolls — measured with a ResizeObserver rather than hard-coded — because SC 2.1.1 needs a scrollable region to be keyboard-reachable, and the unconditional version most implementations ship puts a silent, nameless stop in front of every table that fits. role, aria-labelledby and tabIndex are applied together or not at all: a named region nobody can reach is as useless as a reachable one with no name.

migration.manual: No caller changes required; `fixed` remains the default and every existing column definition behaves as before. The one behavioural change is that a grid wider than its frame now scrolls instead of being clipped — if you wrapped a Table in your own scroll container to work around that, the wrapper is now redundant and will produce a nested scroll area.
